lanes.label: The call and the foe from the north
Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Jeremiah: overview
nodes.d: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth, receives the word of the LORD from the thirteenth year of Josiah to the exile after Zedekiah's eleventh year, warning Judah of judgment from the north and promising restoration and a new covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Jeremiah was and during whose reigns the word of the LORD came to him according to Jeremiah 1:1-3?
ev: Name the kings during whose reigns the word came (Jeremiah 1:1-3)
Explain that the book is not arranged only in the order of the events it describes, using examples from its dates

nodes.t: The call of Jeremiah
nodes.d: The LORD tells Jeremiah he knew and set him apart before birth as a prophet to the nations; Jeremiah protests he is a child, the LORD touches his mouth and gives visions of an almond rod and a boiling pot from the north.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jeremiah was called and how the LORD answered his fear in Jeremiah 1:6-8?
ev: Retell what the LORD says before Jeremiah's birth (1:5)
Describe how the LORD answers Jeremiah's objection (1:6-9)
Explain the two visions of 1:11-16

nodes.t: Israel forsakes the fountain of living waters
nodes.d: The LORD remembers Israel's devotion in the wilderness, charges that the fathers and leaders went after vanity, and says his people committed two evils: forsaking him and digging broken cisterns.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the picture of the fountain and the broken cisterns in Jeremiah 2:13?
ev: Say what the LORD remembers in Jeremiah 2:2-3
Explain the two evils of 2:13
List the people the LORD charges in 2:8, 26

nodes.t: Return, backsliding Israel
nodes.d: Using the image of an unfaithful wife, the LORD calls faithless Israel and Judah to return, promises shepherds after his heart and a gathering to Jerusalem, and calls Judah to circumcise their hearts.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the LORD's call to return in Jeremiah 3:12-14, 3:22 and 4:1-4?
ev: Say what happened to backsliding Israel and what Judah did (3:6-11)
Quote the invitation in 3:12-14
Explain the call to circumcise the heart in 4:4

nodes.t: Disaster from the north
nodes.d: A trumpet is blown for a destroyer coming from the north; Jeremiah laments over the false peace and sees the earth returned to emptiness, though the LORD says he will not make a full end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jeremiah sees in Jeremiah 4:23-26 and what the LORD says in 4:27?
ev: Describe the warning given in Jeremiah 4:5-8
Describe Jeremiah's vision of 4:23-26
Say what the LORD says in 4:27

nodes.t: Not one to be found: Jerusalem's guilt
nodes.d: The LORD asks whether a single just person can be found in Jerusalem, charges leaders and people with false oaths, deceit and ignoring the poor, and says a distant nation will come, yet he will not make a full end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD asks Jeremiah to look for in Jerusalem in chapter 5 and what he finds?
ev: Say what is asked in Jeremiah 5:1
Describe the charges in 5:26-28
Describe the coming nation (5:15-17) and what remains true (5:18)

nodes.t: Jerusalem besieged: peace, peace, when there is no peace
nodes.d: The LORD calls for a siege against Jerusalem, whose people reject his word; prophets and priests heal the wound lightly, saying peace, and the people refuse the old paths; Jeremiah is set as an assayer of metal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the people answer when the LORD points them to the old paths in Jeremiah 6:16?
ev: Quote the false message in Jeremiah 6:14
Say what the LORD invites in 6:16 and the people's reply
Describe the assayer image (6:27-30)

nodes.t: The temple sermon
nodes.d: At the gate of the LORD's house Jeremiah says not to trust "the temple of the LORD"; the LORD cites Shiloh, forbids Jeremiah to pray for the people, and condemns worship of the queen of heaven and child burning in Tophet.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jeremiah told the people not to trust in the temple of the LORD in Jeremiah 7:1-15?
ev: Explain what the people trusted and what the LORD required (7:3-7)
Say how the LORD compares the temple to Shiloh (7:12-14)
Describe the sins at Tophet (7:30-34)

nodes.t: Is there no balm in Gilead?
nodes.d: The people hold to deceit and refuse to return; wise men have rejected the LORD's word; the harvest is past and they are not saved, and Jeremiah weeps asking whether there is no balm in Gilead.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the question Jeremiah asks in 8:22 and why he asks it?
ev: Describe how even the stork knows her times (8:7)
Quote the question of 8:22
Describe the people's complaint in 8:20

nodes.t: Weeping prophet; let him glory that he knows me
nodes.d: Jeremiah longs to weep for the slain of his people, who speak deceit; the LORD announces desolation and says the wise, mighty and rich should not glory in those things but in knowing him as one who exercises lovingkindness, judgment and righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says a person should glory in according to Jeremiah 9:23-24?
ev: Quote Jeremiah 9:1
Say what the LORD says to glory in (9:23-24)
Explain 9:25-26

nodes.t: The living God and the idols of the nations
nodes.d: The LORD says not to learn the way of the nations; idols made by craftsmen cannot speak or move, while the LORD is the true, living God and everlasting king who made the earth by his power.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the idols of the nations with the LORD in Jeremiah 10:3-16?
ev: Describe how the idol is made (10:3-5)
Contrast the LORD and the idols (10:10-16)
Describe Jeremiah's prayer in 10:23-25

nodes.t: The words of this covenant and the plot at Anathoth
nodes.d: Jeremiah is told to proclaim the words of the covenant commanded when Israel left Egypt; Judah has broken it and the LORD forbids prayer for them; Jeremiah learns the men of Anathoth plot against his life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what covenant Jeremiah 11:1-8 refers to and why Judah is said to have broken it?
ev: Say what covenant the LORD refers to and when it was given (11:3-5)
Describe how Judah broke it (11:9-10)
Describe the plot against Jeremiah and the LORD's answer (11:18-23)

nodes.t: Why does the way of the wicked prosper?
nodes.d: Jeremiah asks why the wicked prosper; the LORD says his trouble will grow, grieves over forsaking his heritage, judges Judah's neighbours, and promises compassion and return if the nations learn his ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jeremiah asks the LORD in 12:1 and how the LORD answers in 12:5?
ev: Quote Jeremiah's question (12:1)
Describe the LORD's reply (12:5)
Say what is promised for the nations after plucking out (12:14-17)

nodes.t: The ruined linen belt
nodes.d: Jeremiah buys a linen belt, hides it by the Euphrates, and finds it ruined; the LORD says he will ruin the pride of Judah, warns of exile, and asks whether a leopard can change its spots.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the sign of the linen belt and say what it stood for in Jeremiah 13?
ev: Retell what Jeremiah does with the belt (13:1-7)
Explain what the belt represents (13:9-11)
Quote the question in 13:23

nodes.t: Drought, false prophets and intercession refused
nodes.d: During a drought Jeremiah prays for Judah and the people confess sin, but the LORD says not to pray for them; he denounces prophets who promise peace and Jeremiah weeps for the slain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why the LORD tells Jeremiah not to pray for the people in Jeremiah 14:10-12?
ev: Describe the drought and the people's prayer (14:1-9, 19-22)
Say what the LORD says about the prophets (14:13-16)

nodes.t: Though Moses and Samuel stood before me
nodes.d: The LORD says even Moses and Samuel could not turn him from Judah; he appoints four kinds of destroyers, Jeremiah complains of his pain, and the LORD tells him to return and promises he will be a bronze wall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jeremiah says about the LORD's words in 15:16 and what the LORD promises him in 15:19-21?
ev: Say whom the LORD names in Jeremiah 15:1
Quote Jeremiah's words about God's words in 15:16
Say what the LORD promises Jeremiah in 15:19-21

nodes.t: A prophet forbidden to marry or mourn
nodes.d: Jeremiah is told not to marry, mourn or feast because the LORD will remove peace from the land; the LORD says the people forsook him, promises a return from the north greater than the exodus, and sends fishers and hunters.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jeremiah is forbidden to marry or join mourners in Jeremiah 16?
ev: Say what Jeremiah is told not to do and why (16:2-9)
Describe the promise in 16:14-15

nodes.t: Cursed is the man who trusts in man
nodes.d: The LORD contrasts the person who trusts in man with the one who trusts in the LORD, says the heart is deceitful, and Jeremiah prays for healing; the LORD adds a call to keep the sabbath, promising kings on David's throne if they obey.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the person who trusts in man with the one who trusts in the LORD in Jeremiah 17:5-8?
ev: Contrast the two people and their trees (17:5-8)
Quote 17:9-10
Say what is promised and warned about the sabbath (17:19-27)

nodes.t: The potter and the clay
nodes.d: Jeremiah watches a potter remake a spoiled vessel; the LORD says he can do the same with Israel and will relent of judgment or blessing depending on how a nation responds; the people say there is no hope and plot against Jeremiah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the potter and clay story and say what the LORD says he does when a nation turns from evil in Jeremiah 18:7-8?
ev: Retell what Jeremiah sees at the potter's house (18:1-4)
Explain the message of 18:7-10
Describe the people's reaction (18:12, 18)

nodes.t: The broken jar in the valley of Hinnom
nodes.d: Jeremiah breaks a potter's flask in the valley of Hinnom before elders as a sign the LORD will break the city for idolatry and child sacrifice, and then repeats the warning in the temple court.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Jeremiah does with the flask in Jeremiah 19 and what it means?
ev: Retell the sign Jeremiah performs (19:1-2, 10-11)
Say why the LORD judges (19:4-5)

nodes.t: Pashur strikes Jeremiah; Jeremiah's complaint
nodes.d: Pashur the priest beats Jeremiah and puts him in stocks; Jeremiah names him Terror on every side and tells of exile to Babylon, then complains that the word is like fire in his bones and curses the day of his birth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Jeremiah responds to Pashur and what Jeremiah says about holding back the word in 20:9?
ev: Retell what Pashur does and what Jeremiah says (20:1-6)
Describe the fire in Jeremiah's bones (20:9)
Compare the praise of 20:11-13 with the lament of 20:14-18

nodes.t: Zedekiah asks Jeremiah to enquire of the LORD
nodes.d: When Nebuchadnezzar attacks, King Zedekiah sends to Jeremiah, who answers that the LORD himself will fight against the city and sets before the people the way of life, which is to go out to the Chaldeans, and the way of death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how the LORD answers Zedekiah in Jeremiah 21 and what choice the people are given?
ev: Say who sends to Jeremiah and why (21:1-2)
Describe the LORD's answer (21:4-7)
Describe the two ways set before the people (21:8-9)

nodes.t: Judgment on the sons of Josiah and Coniah
nodes.d: The house of David is told to do justice or the palace will be desolate; Jehoiakim, who built his house by unrighteousness, and Coniah are condemned, with Shallum's exile also announced.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast what the LORD says of Josiah and of Jehoiakim in Jeremiah 22:13-17?
ev: Say what the king is told to do (22:3)
Contrast Jehoiakim with his father Josiah (22:13-17)
Describe what is said of Coniah (22:24-30)

nodes.t: A righteous Branch raised up to David
nodes.d: The LORD condemns the shepherds who scatter his flock, promises to gather the remnant and set shepherds over them, and says he will raise to David a righteous Branch, a king named The LORD our righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises to raise up for David in Jeremiah 23:5-6?
ev: Describe what the LORD promises in Jeremiah 23:3-4
Quote the promise of 23:5-6
Compare 23:7-8 with the exodus

nodes.t: Against the prophets who speak their own dreams
nodes.d: The LORD says the prophets of Samaria and Jerusalem are profane, speak visions of their own heart and dreams without being sent, while his word is like fire and a hammer, and mocks use of "the burden of the LORD."
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD says to tell a true prophet from a false one in Jeremiah 23:16-32?
ev: Say what the LORD says false prophets lack (23:18, 21-22)
Contrast the chaff and the wheat (23:28)
Quote 23:29

nodes.t: Two baskets of figs
nodes.d: After Nebuchadnezzar carries off Jeconiah, Jeremiah is shown a basket of good figs and a basket of bad figs; the LORD says the exiles are the good figs he will return and plant, while Zedekiah and the rest are the bad.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the vision of the two baskets of figs in Jeremiah 24 and what each stands for?
ev: Retell the vision (24:1-3)
Say what the LORD promises the good figs (24:5-7)
Say who the bad figs are (24:8-10)

nodes.t: Seventy years and the cup of wrath
nodes.d: In Jehoiakim's fourth year Jeremiah reminds Judah of twenty-three years of unheeded warnings; Babylon will rule seventy years and then be punished, and the nations are made to drink the cup of the LORD's fury.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jeremiah 25:11-12 says about seventy years and what happens to Babylon afterward?
ev: Say how long Jeremiah had spoken (25:3)
Say what the LORD says about the seventy years (25:11-12)
Describe the cup the nations drink (25:15-29)

nodes.t: Jeremiah on trial
nodes.d: Jeremiah's warning at the temple that the house will become like Shiloh leads priests and prophets to demand his death; the princes and elders spare him, citing Micah in Hezekiah's day, while Urijah is killed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell why Jeremiah was not put to death in Jeremiah 26?
ev: Say what Jeremiah says in the temple court (26:2-6)
Retell the argument for sparing him (26:16-19)
Say what happened to Urijah (26:20-23)

nodes.t: The yoke and the king of Babylon
nodes.d: Jeremiah wears wooden yokes and sends word to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Zidon and to Zedekiah that the LORD has given the lands to Nebuchadnezzar; they are not to heed prophets who say otherwise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jeremiah told the kings and Zedekiah to do in Jeremiah 27 and why he said not to listen to the other prophets?
ev: Describe the sign Jeremiah is told to make (27:2)
Say what the LORD says about serving the king of Babylon (27:6-8, 11-12)
Say what happens to the temple vessels (27:19-22)

nodes.t: Hananiah breaks the yoke
nodes.d: The prophet Hananiah says in the LORD's name that Babylon's yoke will be broken within two years and breaks Jeremiah's yoke; Jeremiah answers that the LORD has made a yoke of iron, and Hananiah dies that year.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the confrontation between Jeremiah and Hananiah and how it ended in Jeremiah 28?
ev: Retell Hananiah's prophecy and what he does to the yoke (28:1-4, 10-11)
Say how Jeremiah says a prophet of peace is known (28:9)
Say what happens to Hananiah (28:15-17)

nodes.t: Jeremiah's letter to the exiles
nodes.d: Jeremiah writes to those carried to Babylon to build houses, plant gardens, seek the city's peace, and wait seventy years, promising thoughts of peace and that they will find the LORD if they seek him with all their heart; false prophets among them are condemned.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jeremiah told the exiles to do in Babylon and what the LORD promised in Jeremiah 29:10-14?
ev: List what the exiles are told to do (29:5-7)
Say what is promised after seventy years (29:10-14)
Describe the warning about false prophets (29:8-9, 21-32)

nodes.t: The time of Jacob's trouble and restoration
nodes.d: The LORD tells Jeremiah to write in a book that he will bring Israel and Judah back; though their wound is incurable because of their sins, he will heal them, break the yoke, and raise up David their king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises Israel and Judah in Jeremiah 30:3, 10 and 17?
ev: Say what Jeremiah is told to write (30:2-3)
Describe the time of Jacob's trouble and the promise (30:7-11)
Quote the covenant words in 30:22

nodes.t: Everlasting love: Israel gathered and Rachel comforted
nodes.d: The LORD loves Israel with an everlasting love and will gather them from the north, redeem them and turn mourning to joy; Rachel weeps for her children but the LORD promises they will return, and the new thing and the sour grape saying are addressed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises in Jeremiah 31:3 and 31:15-17?
ev: Quote Jeremiah 31:3
Describe Rachel's weeping and the promise (31:15-17)
Explain the saying about the sour grape that will no longer be used (31:29-30)

nodes.t: The new covenant
nodes.d: The LORD promises a new covenant with Israel and Judah, unlike the one broken after the exodus: he will write his law on their hearts, they will all know him, and he will forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what is new about the covenant promised in Jeremiah 31:31-34?
ev: Say whom the covenant is made with and what it is unlike (31:31-32)
Describe what the LORD does in 31:33
Quote the promise of forgiveness in 31:34

nodes.t: As sure as the sun and moon: Israel's future and the city rebuilt
nodes.d: The LORD says Israel would cease only if the fixed order of sun, moon and stars departed, and that he will not cast off Israel for their sin; Jerusalem will be rebuilt and holy to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the comparison the LORD makes in Jeremiah 31:35-37?
ev: Say the comparisons the LORD makes in Jeremiah 31:35-37
Describe the rebuilt city (31:38-40)

nodes.t: Jeremiah buys a field at Anathoth
nodes.d: With Jerusalem besieged and Jeremiah imprisoned, the LORD has him buy his cousin's field as a sign that fields will again be bought in the land; Jeremiah prays, and the LORD promises an everlasting covenant and return.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell why Jeremiah bought a field in Anathoth during the siege and what the LORD said about it in Jeremiah 32?
ev: Retell how Jeremiah buys the field and seals the deed (32:6-15)
Quote the LORD's question in 32:27
Describe the promise in 32:37-44

nodes.t: The Branch of righteousness and the covenant with David and the Levites
nodes.d: The LORD promises healing, cleansing and rejoicing, and that a Branch of righteousness will grow up for David; he compares his covenant with David and the Levites to his covenant of day and night.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises about David and the Levites in Jeremiah 33:17-22?
ev: Say what the LORD promises in Jeremiah 33:6-11
Describe the Branch and the name given in 33:15-16
Explain the comparison in 33:20-22

nodes.t: Zedekiah's covenant to free slaves is broken
nodes.d: During the siege Zedekiah and the people covenant to free Hebrew servants, then take them back; the LORD recalls the covenant at the exodus and says that those who passed between the parts of the calf will be given to their enemies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the people did wrong with their servants in Jeremiah 34 and why the LORD judged them?
ev: Say what the king and people covenanted and what they did next (34:8-11)
Say what law the LORD cites from the time of the exodus (34:13-14)
Describe the judgment (34:17-22)

nodes.t: The Rechabites' obedience
nodes.d: In Jehoiakim's days Jeremiah offers wine to the Rechabites, who refuse because their father Jonadab commanded them; the LORD contrasts their obedience to a human father with Judah's refusal to hear him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the Rechabites and say what the LORD teaches through them in Jeremiah 35?
ev: Retell what Jeremiah does and what the Rechabites say (35:5-10)
Explain the LORD's lesson from them (35:13-16)
Say what is promised to the Rechabites (35:18-19)

nodes.t: The scroll burned by Jehoiakim
nodes.d: The LORD has Jeremiah dictate all his words to Baruch, who reads them in the temple and to the princes; King Jehoiakim cuts and burns the scroll piece by piece, and the LORD has Jeremiah write it again with more added.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jeremiah's scroll was written, burned and written again in Jeremiah 36?
ev: Retell how the scroll is written and read (36:1-10)
Describe the king's response (36:21-26)
Say what the LORD commands next (36:27-32)

nodes.t: Jeremiah imprisoned during the siege
nodes.d: When the Chaldeans withdraw briefly because of Pharaoh's army, Jeremiah says they will return and burn the city; he is arrested, accused of deserting, beaten and imprisoned, then secretly questioned by Zedekiah and moved to the court of the prison.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell why Jeremiah was arrested in Jeremiah 37 and what he said to Zedekiah?
ev: Say what Jeremiah says about the Chaldeans' withdrawal (37:7-10)
Describe his arrest (37:11-15)
Say what he asks Zedekiah (37:17-21)

nodes.t: Jeremiah in the cistern and Ebed-melech
nodes.d: The princes lower Jeremiah into a muddy cistern to die; Ebed-melech the Ethiopian pleads with the king and lifts him out with ropes and rags; Zedekiah again questions Jeremiah, who urges him to surrender, and later the LORD promises Ebed-melech deliverance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Ebed-melech helped Jeremiah and what the LORD said to him in Jeremiah 39:15-18?
ev: Retell why the princes put Jeremiah in the cistern (38:1-6)
Retell how Ebed-melech rescues him (38:7-13)
Say what the LORD promises Ebed-melech (39:15-18)

nodes.t: The fall of Jerusalem and Jeremiah freed
nodes.d: In Zedekiah's eleventh year the city is breached; Zedekiah flees, is caught, sees his sons killed and is blinded and taken to Babylon; the city is burned, and Nebuchadnezzar orders that Jeremiah be treated well.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened to Zedekiah and Jerusalem in Jeremiah 39:1-10 and what happened to Jeremiah?
ev: Retell what happens to Zedekiah (39:4-7)
Say what happens to the city and to the poor (39:8-10)
Say how Jeremiah is treated (39:11-14)

nodes.t: Gedaliah governor and his murder
nodes.d: Nebuzaradan releases Jeremiah, who joins Gedaliah at Mizpah; Jews return and gather harvest, but Ishmael murders Gedaliah and others and Johanan and the captains flee toward Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened to Gedaliah and the people at Mizpah in Jeremiah 40-41?
ev: Say what Nebuzaradan says to Jeremiah (40:2-5)
Describe the warning Gedaliah ignores (40:13-16)
Retell what Ishmael does (41:1-10)

nodes.t: Do not go down to Egypt
nodes.d: The remnant asks Jeremiah to pray for guidance and promises to obey, but when the LORD says to stay and he will build them up, and that going to Egypt means the sword and famine, they accuse Jeremiah of lying and go to Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what the remnant asked Jeremiah and how they responded to the LORD's answer in Jeremiah 42-43?
ev: Say what the people promise and what the LORD answers (42:5-12)
Say what the LORD warns about Egypt (42:13-22)
Describe the people's reaction (43:1-7)

nodes.t: Nebuchadnezzar and the stones at Tahpanhes
nodes.d: In Tahpanhes in Egypt Jeremiah hides great stones in the brickwork at Pharaoh's house as a sign that Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne there and strike Egypt and burn the Egyptian gods' temples.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the sign with the stones at Tahpanhes and what it means in Jeremiah 43:8-13?
ev: Describe the sign Jeremiah performs (43:9)
Say what it signifies (43:10-13)

nodes.t: The Jews in Egypt and the queen of heaven
nodes.d: Jeremiah warns the Jews in Egypt that idolatry caused the fall of Jerusalem; the people reply they will keep burning incense to the queen of heaven, and the LORD declares he will watch over them for evil and gives a sign concerning Pharaoh Hophra.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the Jews in Egypt answered Jeremiah in 44:15-19 and how Jeremiah replied?
ev: Say what the people answer Jeremiah (44:15-19)
Say how Jeremiah replies (44:21-23)
Describe the sign in 44:29-30

nodes.t: A word to Baruch
nodes.d: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim the LORD answers Baruch's complaint of sorrow by saying he will break down what he has built, and tells Baruch not to seek great things, promising his life as a prize.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD told Baruch in Jeremiah 45:4-5?
ev: Say what Baruch complained of (45:3)
Say what the LORD tells him to stop seeking and promises (45:5)

nodes.t: Oracles against Egypt and the Philistines
nodes.d: The LORD announces defeat of Pharaoh Necho's army at Carchemish and later Nebuchadnezzar's attack on Egypt, while Jacob is told not to fear; waters from the north overflow the Philistines.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD announces against Egypt in Jeremiah 46 and what comfort he gives Israel?
ev: Describe the defeat of Egypt's army (46:2-12)
Say what the LORD tells Jacob (46:27-28)
Describe the flood from the north against the Philistines (47:2-7)

nodes.t: The oracle against Moab
nodes.d: Moab is to be destroyed because it trusted in its works and treasures and magnified itself against the LORD; Jeremiah mourns for Moab, yet the LORD says he will restore Moab's captivity in the latter days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why Moab is judged in Jeremiah 48 and what is promised at the end?
ev: Say why Moab is judged (48:7, 26, 42)
Describe the mourning (48:31-36)
Say what is promised in 48:47

nodes.t: Oracles against Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar and Elam
nodes.d: The LORD judges Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar and Hazor and Elam; Edom's pride and refuge in the rocks will not save it, orphans and widows of Edom are told to trust him, and captivity of Ammon and Elam will later be restored.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the nations judged in Jeremiah 49 and describe Edom's fate?
ev: Describe the charge against Edom (49:7-16)
Say what happens to Kedar and Hazor (49:28-33)
Say what is promised for Ammon and Elam (49:6, 39)

nodes.t: The fall of Babylon and the return of Israel
nodes.d: The LORD declares through Jeremiah that Babylon will fall to a nation from the north, that Israel and Judah will return weeping and join themselves to the LORD in a perpetual covenant, and that Babylon will be destroyed as Sodom was.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jeremiah 50-51 says will happen to Babylon and to Israel?
ev: Describe how Babylon falls (50:2-3, 51:30-32)
Describe the return of Israel and Judah (50:4-5, 19-20)
Say why the LORD judges Babylon (50:11, 24, 51:24)

nodes.t: The Babylon scroll sunk in the Euphrates
nodes.d: Jeremiah writes all the evil coming on Babylon in a book and tells Seraiah to read it in Babylon, then tie a stone to it and sink it in the Euphrates, saying Babylon shall sink and not rise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Seraiah was to do with the book in Babylon and what the act meant?
ev: Retell what Seraiah is told to do with the book (51:61-64)

nodes.t: The fall of Jerusalem and the exiles recounted
nodes.d: The book closes with Zedekiah's rebellion, the siege, the burning of the temple, the stripping of the bronze pillars and vessels, the executions at Riblah, the numbers carried to Babylon, and Jehoiachin's release and honour in Babylon.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the fall of Jerusalem in Jeremiah 52 and how the chapter ends with Jehoiachin?
ev: Retell the fall of Jerusalem (52:4-14)
Say what is taken from the temple (52:17-23)
Describe what happens to Jehoiachin (52:31-34)

nodes.t: Lamentations: overview
nodes.d: Five poems mourn the desolation of Jerusalem, confess that the LORD afflicted her for her transgressions, and in the middle chapter turn to hope in the LORD's mercies, ending with a prayer for restoration.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Lamentations mourns and which verses in chapter 3 express hope?
ev: Say what the five chapters of Lamentations are about
Name the hopeful turning point in the book (3:21-26)

nodes.t: Ezekiel: overview
nodes.d: Ezekiel the priest, among the captives by the river Chebar in the fifth year of Jehoiachin's captivity, sees the glory of the LORD, announces the fall of Jerusalem, speaks against the nations, and sees promises of restoration and a new temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say where Ezekiel was and what the first chapter says happened to him?
ev: Say where and when Ezekiel received the word (1:1-3)
Describe the main movement of the book from judgment to restoration using the texts

nodes.t: The soul that sins shall die
nodes.d: The LORD rejects the proverb that fathers eat sour grapes and children's teeth are set on edge, saying each soul that sins dies, a person is judged by his own life, and the wicked who turn live; he has no pleasure in the death of the wicked.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Ezekiel 18 says about children bearing their fathers' guilt and about the wicked who turn?
ev: Say what proverb is rejected (18:2-3)
Describe the cases of the just father, wicked son and righteous grandson (18:5-18)

nodes.t: I will sprinkle clean water and give a new heart and spirit
nodes.d: The LORD says he will act for his holy name, not Israel's sake: he will gather them, sprinkle clean water on them, give a new heart and put his Spirit within them so they keep his statutes, and make the land like Eden.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the LORD promises to do in Ezekiel 36:24-28?
ev: Say why the LORD acts (36:21-23)
List what he promises in 36:24-28
Describe the land after cleansing (36:33-36)

nodes.t: Daniel: overview
nodes.d: Daniel and his friends are taken to Babylon, serve under Babylonian and Persian kings, and are delivered in the furnace and lions' den; Daniel interprets dreams and receives visions of kingdoms, the Ancient of days, and the end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name Daniel and his three friends and say how the book of Daniel is arranged?
ev: Name Daniel and his three friends with their Babylonian names (1:6-7)
Say which kings Daniel served (1:21, 5:31, 6:28)
Describe the two halves of the book: stories (1-6) and visions (7-12)

nodes.t: Daniel's prayer of confession
nodes.d: Reading in Jeremiah that Jerusalem's desolation would last seventy years, Daniel prays with fasting, confessing that Israel has sinned and not heeded the prophets, that the curse written in the law of Moses has come, and asks God to act for his own name's sake.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what prompted Daniel's prayer in Daniel 9:2 and what he confesses?
ev: Say what Daniel understood from the books (9:2)
List elements of his confession (9:5-14)
Say on what ground he asks God to hear (9:16-19)

nodes.t: Matthew: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.t: Flight to Egypt and return to Nazareth
nodes.d: Warned in dreams, Joseph takes the child to Egypt away from Herod, who has the children of Bethlehem killed; after Herod dies the family returns and settles in Nazareth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the escape from Herod and where the family finally lived?
ev: Trace the family’s journey: Bethlehem, Egypt, Nazareth
Name the three places where Matthew says a prophecy was fulfilled (2:15, 17-18, 23)

nodes.t: Cleansing the temple
nodes.d: Jesus drives out the buyers and sellers, overturns tables and seats, says the house of prayer has become a den of thieves, heals the blind and lame, and answers the priests about children’s praise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus overturned the tables?
ev: Say what Jesus did and quoted
Describe what the children cried and the priests’ reaction

nodes.t: Mark: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Mark, from “the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1) through Jesus’ ministry in Galilee, the road to Jerusalem and his death, to the empty tomb and commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Mark is about and where it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: John and the start of ministry (1), Galilee (1-8), the way to Jerusalem (8-10), the last week and passion (11-15), the empty tomb (16)
Say what Mark calls the book in 1:1

nodes.t: The fig tree and the cleansing of the temple
nodes.d: Jesus curses a leafy fig tree without fruit, drives out sellers and moneychangers saying the house is for prayer for all nations, and next day the disciples see the fig tree withered; he teaches faith and forgiving when praying.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did in the temple and what he taught about prayer?
ev: Retell the order of events
Say what Jesus taught about prayer

nodes.t: Jesus Drives Out the Traders
nodes.d: Jesus enters the temple and drives out those selling, saying his house is a house of prayer but they made it a den of thieves, and teaches there daily while the chief priests seek to destroy him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Jesus did in the temple and what he said about it?
ev: Say what Jesus did in the temple and what he said.

nodes.t: The cross: God's wisdom and power
nodes.d: Paul says the preaching of the cross looks foolish to those perishing but is the power of God to those being saved, and that God chose the weak and low so that no one may boast.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says the cross is God's wisdom and power, using 1 Corinthians 1:18-31?
ev: Contrast how the cross is seen by those perishing and by those saved (1:18)
List who God chose according to 1:26-29 and why (1:29)
Name what Christ is made to us (1:30)

nodes.t: 2 Corinthians: overview
nodes.d: Paul's second letter to the Corinthians: comfort in affliction, the ministry of the new covenant and reconciliation, the collection for the saints, and a defence of his apostleship (1:1-13:14).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 2 Corinthians and say what its three main parts are about?
ev: Name the main sections: comfort and ministry (1-7), the collection (8-9), Paul's defence of his apostleship (10-13)
Say what Paul tells the Corinthians about his sufferings

nodes.t: Ministers of the new covenant
nodes.d: Paul says the Corinthians are Christ's letter written by the Spirit on hearts, calls himself a minister of the new testament, and contrasts the ministry of death carved on stone, with its fading glory, with the ministry of the Spirit and righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul contrasts the ministry written on stone with the ministry of the Spirit in 2 Corinthians 3:3-11?
ev: Say what the Corinthians are called in 3:2-3
Explain the difference between the letter and the Spirit (3:6)
Compare the two ministrations in 3:7-11

nodes.t: A better covenant: the new covenant promised
nodes.d: Jesus ministers in the true tabernacle as mediator of a better covenant on better promises; the writer cites the promise of a new covenant, in which God will write his laws on hearts, be their God, and remember their sins no more, making the first old.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the writer says God promised in the new covenant (8:8-12)?
ev: State what is better about the covenant (8:6)
List the promises of 8:10-12
Say what 8:13 says about the first covenant

nodes.t: One sacrifice for sins for ever
nodes.d: The law's repeated sacrifices could not take away sins, but Christ came to do God's will and by one offering of his body perfected for ever those who are sanctified; the writer again cites the covenant promise that sins will be remembered no more.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Christ's single offering is enough according to Hebrews 10:10-18?
ev: Say why the old sacrifices were repeated (10:1-4)
State what Christ did and where he sat down (10:10-14)

nodes.t: Hebrews: overview
nodes.d: The letter to the Hebrews presents Jesus as God's Son, greater than angels and Moses, our great high priest after Melchizedek who mediates a better covenant by one sacrifice, and calls readers to faith and endurance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Hebrews teaches about Jesus and what the readers are told to do?
ev: Describe the main parts: the Son (1-2), Moses and rest (3-4), the high priest (4-7), the new covenant and sacrifice (8-10), faith (11), endurance and exhortations (12-13)

nodes.t: The woman on the scarlet beast
nodes.d: An angel shows John the judgment of the great whore, Babylon the great, seated on a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns and drunk with the blood of the saints; the angel explains the mystery and says the Lamb will overcome the beast's allies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what John sees in Revelation 17 and what the angel explains?
ev: Describe the woman and the beast
Say what the angel says the waters and the woman are in 17:15, 18
Say what 17:14 says about the Lamb
